text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sarajevo press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Bosnia's Moslem-Croat Federation parliament session has been blocked by a boycott of Croat Democratic Union (HDZ) delegates, an official from opposition Socialist Democratic Party says, emphasising that such a move could bring Bosnia back to the status of war.

- Moslem-Croat Federation Government will use its own money to support return of displaced people and reconstruction of houses in the disputed north Bosnian town of Brcko which is the key for future development of the Federation, Prime Minister Edhem Bicakcic says.

- President of the Moslem-Croat Federation, Kresimir Zubak, will consider sacking of Deputy Prime Minister Drago Bilandzija only after he answers to allegations that he allowed a private company to avoid paying millions of dollars worth of taxes in Croat-controlled territory.
- Defence Minister of Bosnia's Moslem-Croat Federation, Ante Jelavic, says there is a dispute between the partners over how many soldiers of either nationality the Federation army should have.
- Unpaid medical workers in the central Bosnian town of Zenica went on strike on Wednesday, the director of the town's main hospital says.

- Bosnia's Serb republic will not hand over its indicted war criminals to the International Criminal Tribunal in the Hague, Bosnian deputy foreign affairs minister, Dragan Bozanic, a Serb, tells Serb republic television.

- Since Croat demand for election of Bosnia's Moslem-Croat Federation president and vice-president has not been met yet, the Croat deputies could not participate in the Federation parliament session, secretary-general of Croatian Democratic Union (HDZ) party, Srecko Vucina, says.

- Seventeen patients in the city hospital in northwest Bosnian town of Bihac died over the past 15 days due to lack of medicines, a medical union leader in the area says but a chief doctor in the hospital denies his account.
